newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish shares follow London and Wall Street higher.
newsitem.headline: Irish shares follow London and Wall Street higher.

text.p: The Irish share price index firmed in afternoon trade on Tuesday, following the trend in London and on Wall Street, dealers said.
"The market is in quite good nick today. We have seen a good recovery, following the international tone, with bargain-hunting at the lower levels," one trader said.
By 1555 GMT, the ISEQ index of Irish shares was up 28.15 points or 0.78 percent at 3,642.79. In London, the FTSE 100 closed 79.2 points higher, while in New York the Dow was up 62 points.
Dealers said volume in Dublin was reasonable and there had been a broad spread of interest in the Irish market.
Building materials group CRH gained 12 pence to 738, while Smurfit was up seven pence at 231.
Kerry Group surged 30 pence to 710 and Fyffes added three pence to 101.
In the financial sector, Allied Irish Banks was up 1.5 pence at 590, Bank of Ireland held steady at 790, while Irish Life added 16 pence to 348.
Heading south, however, were Greencore GNC.I which shed five pence to 325, IWP International, off 10 pence to 290 and Jurys, down 15 pence at 400.
Independent Newspapers, whose Australian associate Australian Provincial Newspapers earlier announced a rise in half-year net profit, lost eight pence to 452.
